The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Dan Roman.
President Trump says he's offered
the White House press secretary's job
to Dana White, the CEO of Ultimate Fighting Championship.
NPR's Mara Eliason reports.
It might be no more than trolling,
but Trump posted on Truth Social
that he'd offered the job to White,
saying that White was a quote,
"violent fighter and warrior."
Trump is a longtime friend of White's
and a supporter of the UFC,
which held a mixed martial arts cage match
on the White House lawn to celebrate
the president's 80th birthday in June.
White says he's coming to Washington
to meet with the president on Monday.
Trump has been trying to adjust
to the new shift in power in Washington
after Republicans' dramatic loss in the midterm elections.
Mara Eliason, NPR News.
Stephen Miller is set to take over Monday
as White House chief of staff
replacing Susie Wiles, who resigned Friday.
Miller is the architect of many of President Trump's
more controversial domestic policies,
including immigration reform.
Now many Democrats are saying Trump
made the wrong choice for the position.
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries,
who is expected to become the next speaker
in the next Congress, was on ABCs this week.
It was an irresponsible decision, in my view.
There's not gonna be any opportunity, certainly,
to work with Stephen Miller and what he represents.
And we're committed to forcefully pushing back
against the extremism that they may try
to continue to unleash on the American people.
And we've got a firewall in the House
and a firewall in the Senate,
thanks to the American people.
Jeffries earlier called Miller, quote,
"a malignant tumor," and that President Trump
should fire him instead of promote him.
Russia is stepping up attacks on Ukraine's power grid
ahead of the latest U.S.-mediated talks
in Abu Dhabi this week.
The round of airstrikes has left hundreds
of thousands of people without electric power.
NPR's Eleanor Beardsley reports.
The attacks are part of the Kremlin's strategy
to freeze Ukrainians and leave them in the dark this winter.
A regional military spokesperson
said Ukraine's power company, DTEC,
is working to restore electricity,
but efforts are being hampered
by constant Russian shelling.
Oleksandr Hansa said hospitals had been forced
to switch to diesel generators,
and electric-powered public transport had ground to a halt
in the large eastern city of Nipro.
President Volodymyr Zelensky accused Russia
of seeking to apply maximum pressure
ahead of trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi
in the coming days by, quote,
"plunging the entire country into a blackout."
Russia began stepping up attacks
on Ukrainian energy infrastructure in late September.
It has targeted the sector every winter
since launching its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
Eleanor Beardsley, NPR News, Kyiv.
- Central command since Saturday had fired
on a disabled ship in the Strait of Hormuz
after it did not respond.
This is NPR.
- Pope Leo heads to Argentina for the second leg
of his South American tour after visiting Uruguay.
The Pope became the first leader of the Catholic Church
to visit Uruguay in nearly four decades.
When he attempted to remind the people,
the Catholic Church is a part of their identity as a nation,
even as that country has become deeply, deeply secular.
A strong earthquake hit Central Japan early Sunday.
NPR's Anthony Kuhn reports authorities are warning
of strong aftershocks in the coming days.
- The quake hit just after 1 a.m. local time
and was centered on Central Shizuoka Prefecture
at a depth of 25 miles below the Earth's surface.
Japan's meteorological agency put it at magnitude 5.7,
the U.S. Geological Survey at 5.5.
The quake threw some of the injured off stairs
or from their beds.
It shattered windows and sent merchandise
tumbling from store shelves.
Authorities reported that following the quake,
no changes were detected in the Nankai trough,
a fault line running along Japan's east coast.
Authorities put the chance of a magnitude eight
or nine quake centered on the trough at up to 50 to 90%
depending on the model in the next 30 years.
In a worst case scenario,
that could cause up to 298,000 deaths.
Anthony Kuhn in PR News, Seoul.
- Contract negotiations at the Southern California ports
of Los Angeles and Long Beach
between the unionized maritime security guards
and management have been extended through November the 20th.
Both ports reported all-time cargo volume records
in the month of September.
I'm Dan Roman, NPR News in Washington.
